record.title: Polynomial-time computation of the ν robustness measure
record.statement:
Let $\nu$ denote the paper's robustness measure for systems with structured uncertainties, and let arbitrary precision mean that the computed value can be made to have any prescribed accuracy.

**Polynomial-time computation conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm to compute $\nu$ within arbitrary precision.

Such an algorithm would make the proposed robustness measure computationally tractable for large-scale systems and complement the distributed methods developed for its convex upper bound. The source states this as a concluding research conjecture and supplies no algorithm or proof establishing it.
record.source_name: Olle Kjellqvist and John C. Doyle, “ν-Analysis: A New Notion of Robustness for Large Systems with Structured Uncertainties”, arXiv:2204.05359 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.05359

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The conjectured formula for maximal chordal subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $f(n,m)$ be the largest integer such that every graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges has a chordal subgraph with at least $f(n,m)$ edges. For $k\geq 2$, let $t_k(n)$ denote the number of edges in the balanced complete $k$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. Let $n\geq 1$ and suppose that

$$
t_k(n)+1\leq m\leq t_{k+1}(n).
$$

**The maximal chordal subgraph conjecture.** Then

$$
f(n,m)=\min_{t,r}\bigl(kn-t+r\bigr)-\binom{k+1}{2},
$$

where the minimum is taken over all $t,r\geq 0$ satisfying

$$
t_{k-1}(n-t)+t(n-t)+t_2(r)\geq m.
$$

The paper determines $f(n,m)$ asymptotically for all $m$ and exactly when $m\leq t_3(n)+1$; this conjecture proposes the exact value throughout the remaining ranges of $m$.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner and Benny Sudakov, “Maximal Chordal Subgraphs”, arXiv:2205.08474 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The multi-robber damage conjecture on saving three vertices
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $Delta(G)$, and let $s$ be a positive integer. In the one-cop, $s$-robber damage game, the cop saves $k$ vertices if the optimal damage satisfies $\operatorname{dmg}(G;s)\leq |V(G)|-k$.

**Multi-robber damage conjecture.** For all $s>2$, if

$$
\Delta(G)\geq \binom{s}{2}+2,
$$

then the cop can save three vertices against $s$ robbers.

For two robbers, the corresponding result is known under the weaker condition $\Delta(G)\geq 3$. The conjecture proposes a sufficient maximum-degree condition for saving three vertices with more than two robbers; its status is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Miloš Stojaković and Lasse Wulf, “On the Multi-Robber Damage Number”, arXiv:2209.10965 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.10965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

record.title: McCuaig–Ota conjecture on contractible sets in 3-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-connected graph. A set $W\subset V(G)$ is **contractible** if $G(W)$ is connected and $G-W$ is $2$-connected; a contractible set with $k$ vertices is called a $k$-contractible set. **McCuaig–Ota conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists an integer $n$ such that every $3$-connected graph $G$ on at least $n$ vertices has a $k$-contractible set.

The conjecture asks whether sufficiently large $3$-connected graphs always contain contractible sets of every prescribed finite size. The paper proves the assertion for $k\geqslant 5$ under the minimum-degree condition $\delta(G)\geqslant \left[\frac{2k+1}{3}\right]+2$, while the unrestricted conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nikolai Karol, “Restriction on minimum degree in the contractible sets problem”, arXiv:2212.02079 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1101.2357](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2357).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02079

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: Kim–Kim–Liu's local Ramsey–Turán density conjecture for $(K_3,K_6)$
record.statement:
For $\delta>0$, let $\rho(3,6,\delta)$ be the limiting maximum edge density of an $n$-vertex graph with independence number at most $\delta n$ that admits a red/blue coloring with no red $K_3$ and no blue $K_6$. **Kim–Kim–Liu's conjecture.** For sufficiently small $\delta>0$,

$$
\rho(3,6,\delta)=\frac{5}{12}+\frac{\delta}{2}+2\delta^2.
$$

The source describes the right-hand side as attained by a construction, so the conjecture concerns the matching upper bound for sufficiently small $\delta$.
record.source_name: Xinyu Hu and Qizhong Lin, “Two Ramsey-Turán numbers involving triangles”, arXiv:2212.07234 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.07234

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: The joint Ramsey–Turán density conjecture for $(K_3,K_7)$
record.statement:
For $\delta>0$, let $\rho(3,7,\delta)$ be the limiting maximum edge density of an $n$-vertex graph with independence number at most $\delta n$ that admits a red/blue coloring with no red $K_3$ and no blue $K_7$. **The $(K_3,K_7)$ density conjecture.** For sufficiently small $\delta>0$,

$$
\rho(3,7,\delta)=\frac{7}{16}+\frac{\delta}{2}.
$$

The source gives a construction proving the corresponding lower bound. The conjecture is the assertion that this construction is asymptotically optimal for sufficiently small $\delta$.
record.source_name: Xinyu Hu and Qizhong Lin, “Two Ramsey-Turán numbers involving triangles”, arXiv:2212.07234 (2023).

record.title: Caro–Petru1evski–skrekovski's conflict-free chromatic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)$ be its conflict-free chromatic number, the least number of colours in a proper vertex colouring such that every vertex has a neighbour whose colour occurs exactly once in its neighbourhood.

**Caro–Petru1evski–skrekovski's conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$,

$$
\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)\leq \Delta+1.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the known general upper bound $\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)\leq\left\lfloor 5\Delta/2\right\rfloor$ and is the central conflict-free colouring problem addressed asymptotically in the paper. The text indicates that it is proved when the minimum degree is sufficiently large relative to $\log\Delta$, while the unrestricted case remains open.
record.source_name: Mateusz Kamyczura and Jakub Przybyło, “On conflict-free proper colourings of graphs without small degree vertices”, arXiv:2212.08936 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08936

record.title: Belkhechine et al.'s lower-bound conjecture for the inversion number
record.statement:
For every positive integer $n$, let

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{inv}(D)\mid D\text{ is an oriented graph of order }n\}.
$$

Here $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ is the minimum number of inversions needed to transform $D$ into an acyclic oriented graph.

**Belkhechine et al.'s inversion-number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This strengthens the elementary counting lower bound given immediately before it and asserts that the logarithmic loss in that bound is unnecessary. The source does not state a resolution.

record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09188

record.title: Bang-Jensen et al.'s tightness conjecture for the cycle-transversal bound
record.statement:
Let $\tau(D)$ denote the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion makes an oriented graph $D$ acyclic, and let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ denote its inversion number.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s tightness conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there exists an oriented graph $D$ such that

$$
\tau(D)=n\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{inv}(D)=2n.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the general bound $\operatorname{inv}(D)\leq2\tau(D)$ is tight for every positive value of the cycle-transversal number; the paper notes it would follow from the dijoin conjecture. The source does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Frédéric Havet, Florian Hörsch, Felix Klingelhoefer, Nicolas Nisse, Clément Rambaud and Quentin Vermande, “Problems, proofs, and disproofs on the inversion number”, arXiv:2212.09188 (2022).

record.title: Alon's partition conjecture for inversion number
record.statement:
For an oriented graph $D$ and a vertex subset $V_i$, write $D\langle V_i\rangle$ for the subdigraph induced by $V_i$; let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ denote inversion number.

**Alon's inversion-number partition conjecture.** For every two positive integers $k_1,k_2$, there exists an integer $f(k_1,k_2)$ such that every oriented graph $D$ with

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D)\geq f(k_1,k_2)
$$

 admits a partition $(V_1,V_2)$ of $V(D)$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D\langle V_i\rangle)\geq k_i\quad\text{for }i=1,2.
$$

This asks for an inversion-number analogue of Alon's minimum-out-degree partition conjecture: sufficiently large global inversion number should force both parts to retain prescribed inversion complexity. The source does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Frédéric Havet, Florian Hörsch, Felix Klingelhoefer, Nicolas Nisse, Clément Rambaud and Quentin Vermande, “Problems, proofs, and disproofs on the inversion number”, arXiv:2212.09188 (2022).

record.title: Poonen's twin-free structural formulation
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite union-closed family of sets, and let $M$ be its largest set. Assume that for every pair of elements $a,b\in M$, the family contains a set $A$ with $|A\cap\{a,b\}|=1$. Let $x$ be the only element belonging to at least half of the sets of $\mathcal{F}$. **Poonen's structural conjecture.** If $|M|\geq 2$, then $\mathcal{F}$ consists of $\emptyset$ together with precisely all subsets of $M$ containing $x$; if $|M|=1$, then $\mathcal{F}=\{\{x\}\}$ or $\mathcal{F}=\{\emptyset,\{x\}\}$. This is the equivalent formulation associated with the twin-free condition and is stated as open.
record.source_name: Adam Kabela, Michal Polák and Jakub Teska, “The number of abundant elements in union-closed families without small sets”, arXiv:2212.09279 (2023).

record.title: Coarse-convergence conjecture for Morse boundaries of hierarchically hyperbolic groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a hierarchically hyperbolic group (HHG), and let $\partial_M G$ be its Morse boundary. Assume that $G$ admits a largest acylindrical action. The topology on $\partial_M G$ induced by this action is the topology of coarse convergence of hierarchy paths. **Coarse-convergence conjecture.** The topology on the Morse boundary of an HHG induced by its largest acylindrical action is the topology of coarse convergence of hierarchy paths. Largest acylindrical actions are known to exist for all hierarchically hyperbolic groups and to be $\kappa$-injective, but identifying the induced topology with coarse convergence of hierarchy paths remains open.
record.source_name: Carolyn Abbott and Merlin Incerti-Medici, “Hyperbolic projections and topological invariance of sublinearly Morse boundaries”, arXiv:2212.09539 (2022).

record.title: The weaker Vizing conjecture for layer projections contained in minimum dominating sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G\Box H$ be their Cartesian product, and let $D$ be a dominating set of $G\Box H$. For each $h\in V(H)$, let $G_h$ be the $G$-layer corresponding to $h$, and let $p_G$ denote projection onto $G$. **The weaker Vizing conjecture.** If, for every $h\in V(H)$, there is a minimum dominating set $D_h$ of $G$ such that

$$
p_G(D\cap G_h)\subseteq D_h,
$$

then

$$
|D|\geq \gamma(G)\gamma(H).
$$

This is a special case of Vizing's conjecture, motivated by the paper's discussion of vertically undominated cells and equality in the general half-bound; the paper establishes related special cases but leaves this formulation as the object of conjectural interest.
record.source_name: Simon Špacapan, “A note on Vizing's conjecture”, arXiv:2212.09571 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09571

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: A linear upper bound for the Gaussian Simes-test error probability
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G^K$ denote the class of Gaussian-dependent vectors of $K$ p-values, and let $S_K(\mathbf P)$ be the Simes p-value for $\mathbf P$. Define

$$
s_K(\alpha):=\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal G^K}\mathbb P\bigl(S_K(\mathbf P)\leqslant\alpha\bigr).
$$

**Gaussian Simes bound.** There exists $c\geqslant 1$ such that

$$
s_K(\alpha)\leqslant c\alpha
$$

for all $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $K\in\mathbb N$.
If true, determining the smallest possible $c$, especially for practically relevant small values of $\alpha$, is important. The paper notes that the currently available general bound grows with $K$, so whether a universal constant exists remains open.
record.source_name: Ziyu Chi, Aaditya Ramdas and Ruodu Wang, “Multiple testing under negative dependence”, arXiv:2212.09706 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09706

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2022). “It remains an open question to find a useful upper bound for $ \p( S_K(\mathbf P)\le\alpha)$ over all Gaussian-dependent $\mathbf P\in \mathcal U^K$ for practical values of $\alpha$ such as $0.05$ or $0.1$.”

record.title: Equality of the Gaussian worst-case FDR and Simes error bounds
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G^K$ be the class of Gaussian-dependent vectors of $K$ p-values, and let $S_K(\mathbf P)$ be the Simes p-value. Define

$$
s_K(\alpha):=\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal G^K}\mathbb P\bigl(S_K(\mathbf P)\leqslant\alpha\bigr).
$$

For the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure at level $\alpha$, let $f_K(\alpha)$ be the maximum false discovery rate over the possible numbers of true null hypotheses and Gaussian-dependent p-value vectors.
**Gaussian FDR–Simes equality.**

$$
f_K(\alpha)=s_K(\alpha)
$$

for all $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $K\in\mathbb N$.
The equality would identify the worst-case Gaussian FDR with the worst-case Gaussian Simes-test error probability. The paper explicitly says that it remains unclear whether these quantities are equal, so the claim is open.
record.source_name: Ziyu Chi, Aaditya Ramdas and Ruodu Wang, “Multiple testing under negative dependence”, arXiv:2212.09706 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09706

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2022). “It remains an open question to find a useful upper bound for $ \p( S_K(\mathbf P)\le\alpha)$ over all Gaussian-dependent $\mathbf P\in \mathcal U^K$ for practical values of $\alpha$ such as $0.05$ or $0.1$.”

record.title: Infinitude conjecture for prime exponents in values of $3^{3+6c'}+1$
record.statement:
Let $c'$ range over integers with $c'\not\equiv 3\pmod 7$, and consider the prime factorization of $3^{3+6c'}+1$. 

**Infinitude conjecture.** There are infinitely many values of $c'\not\equiv 3\pmod 7$ such that every prime other than $2$ and $7$ occurring in the factorization of $3^{3+6c'}+1$ has exponent congruent to $1\pmod 3$.

Such values of $c'$ would produce the polynomial families used to construct further twists of the Klein quartic that are counterexamples to the Hasse principle. The source provides no resolution of this arithmetic conjecture.
record.source_name: Elisa Lorenzo García and Michaël Vullers, “Counter-examples to the Hasse principle among the twists of the Klein quartic”, arXiv:2212.10900 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10900

record.title: Horak–AlBdaiwi conjecture on diameter perfect Lee codes
record.statement:
Let $DPL(n,d)$ denote a diameter $d$ perfect Lee code in $\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. For odd $d$, this agrees with a perfect Lee code of radius $(d-1)/2$; for even $d$, it is defined using a tiling by maximum-size anticodes of diameter $d-1$. **Horak–AlBdaiwi conjecture.** There is no $DPL(n,d)$ code for $n\ge3$ and $d>4$, with the exception of the pair

$$
(n,d)=(3,6).
$$
 This is presented as an extension of the Golomb–Welch conjecture. Etzion proposed the problem in 2011, and Horak and AlBdaiwi formally presented the conjecture in 2012; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Tao Zhang and Gennian Ge, “On linear diameter perfect Lee codes with diameter 6”, arXiv:2212.12212 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12212

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: Fingerhut's max-sum matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $S$ be an even set of points in the plane, and let $\{a_ib_i:i=1,\dots,n\}$ be a max-sum matching of $S$, where $|S|=2n$. A point $o$ is required to satisfy, for every matched pair, the sum of its distances to the pair's endpoints. **Fingerhut's conjecture.** There exists a point $o$ in the plane such that

$$
\|a_i-o\|+\|b_i-o\|\leq \frac{2}{\sqrt 3}\|a_i-b_i\|\qquad\text{for all }i=1,\dots,n.
$$

The factor $2/\sqrt 3$ is optimal, and the conjecture was introduced by Andy Fingerhut in connection with minimum Steiner stars; it was previously known with weaker factors and is proved in this paper.
record.source_name: Polina Barabanshchikova and Alexandr Polyanskii, “Intersecting ellipses induced by a max-sum matching”, arXiv:2212.14200 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14200

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Rainbow tight Hamilton cycle conjecture at the minimum degree threshold
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $d$ be positive integers, let $\mu>0$, and let $h_d^{k-1}(k,n)$ be the minimum $d$-degree threshold for a Hamilton tight cycle in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph. Let $\textbf{G}=\{G_i\}_{i\in[n]}$ be a $k$-graph system, and let $\delta_d(G_i)$ denote the minimum $d$-degree of $G_i$.

**Rainbow minimum-threshold conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, if

$$
\delta_d(G_i)\geq h_d^{k-1}(k,n)+\mu\binom{n}{d}
$$

for every $i\in[n]$, then $\textbf{G}$ admits a rainbow Hamilton cycle.

This conjecture proposes that, up to an additive error, the rainbow threshold agrees with the ordinary tight Hamilton-cycle threshold. The source gives no resolution, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Yucong Tang, Bin Wang, Guanghui Wang and Guiying Yan, “Rainbow Hamilton cycle in hypergraph system”, arXiv:2302.00080 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2006.16544](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16544).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00080

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023). “This was recently verified asymptotically by Cheng, Wang and Zhao , and completely by Joos and Kim .”

record.title: Exponent improvement conjecture for even prisms
record.statement:
For each integer $k\geq2$, consider the Cartesian product $C_{2k}\square P_2$ of the cycle $C_{2k}$ and the path $P_2$. The notation $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denotes the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $H$. **Even-prism exponent improvement conjecture.** For every $k\geq2$, there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(k)>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2k}\square P_2)=O\left(n^{\frac53-\varepsilon}\right).
$$

This would improve the currently stated general upper bound $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2k}\square P_2)=O(n^{5/3})$; the paper presents the improvement as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Xiaocong He, Yongtao Li and Lihua Feng, “Extremal graphs for the odd prism”, arXiv:2302.03278 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Gyárfás–Sumner analogue for eta-boundedness
record.statement:
For finite graphs $G$ and $H$, say that $G$ is **$H$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. Write $\omega(G)$ for the clique number and $\eta(G)$ for the minimum size of a set meeting every maximum stable set. A graph class is **$\eta$-bounded** if its members satisfy an upper bound on $\eta$ depending only on clique number.

**Gyárfás–Sumner analogue for $\eta$-boundedness.** For every forest $H$, there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq f(\omega(G))$.

The conjecture is motivated by the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture and is known for stars and induced subgraphs of $P_4$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Sepehr Hajebi, Yanjia Li and Sophie Spirkl, “Hitting all maximum stable sets in P_5-free graphs”, arXiv:2302.04986 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04986

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2023). “This is still open, and might be true as far as we know.”

record.title: Conjecture on the power-series coefficients of the expected largest BP-factorization width
record.statement:
Let $E_k$ denote the limit of the expected width of the largest block-palindrome factorization of a length-$n$ word over an alphabet of size $k$, whose existence is established for every $k\geq 2$. Let $(a_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be the coefficient sequence in the formal expansion in powers of $k^{-1}$. **Coefficient conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, 

$$
E_k=1+\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}a_i k^{-i},
$$

where the sequence $(a_n/2)_{n\geq 1}$ is OEIS sequence A274199. This conjecture identifies the empirically observed coefficients of the expected limiting width; the paper provides numerical evidence but does not establish the claimed coefficient sequence.
record.source_name: Daniel Gabric and Jeffrey Shallit, “Smallest and Largest Block Palindrome Factorizations”, arXiv:2302.13147 (2023).

record.title: Weaker variant of Woodall's dijoin decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph, and let a **dijoin** be a set of arcs meeting every dicut. A set of arcs is a $k$-dijoin if it can be decomposed into $k$ dijoins. Let $\tau\geq 2$ be an integer, and suppose every dicut of $D$ has size at least $\tau$.

**Weaker dijoin decomposition conjecture.** The arc set $A$ can be decomposed into a $k$-dijoin and a $(\tau-k)$-dijoin, for every $k\in\{1,\ldots,\tau-1\}$.

This is presented as a weaker variant of Woodall's conjecture, which asserts that the minimum size of a dicut equals the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dijoins and remains open. The case $k=1$ and $k=\tau-1$ is known, while the intermediate cases remain open.
record.source_name: Ahmad Abdi, Gérard Cornuéjols and Giacomo Zambelli, “Arc connectivity and submodular flows in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.19472 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19472

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Shangguan–Tamo conjecture on limits for hypergraph configurations
record.statement:
Let $f^{(r)}(n;s,k)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no collection of $k$ edges spanning at most $s$ vertices. For positive integers $r$, $k$, and $t$, set $s=k(r-t)+t$. **Shangguan–Tamo conjecture.** For any positive integers $r$, $k$, and $t$, the limit

$$
\pi(r,t,k):=\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} n^{-t} f^{(r)}(n;k(r-t)+t,k)
$$

exists. This generalises the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture, corresponding to $r=3$ and $t=2$; the limit is known in several cases, including all even $k$ when $r$ is sufficiently large relative to $k$ and $t$, and $k\in\{5,7\}$ for all $r>t\ge 2$, but the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Shoham Letzter and Amedeo Sgueglia, “On a problem of Brown, Erdős and Sós”, arXiv:2312.03856 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03856

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Wang–Xu conjecture for very exotic spheres
record.statement: Let a **very exotic sphere** mean a homotopy sphere that does not bound a parallelizable manifold. The preceding results show that very exotic spheres exist in at least $99$ congruence classes of dimensions modulo $192$. **Wang–Xu conjecture.** Very exotic spheres exist in all dimensions greater than $4$, except dimensions $5$, $6$, $11$, $12$, $27$, $43$, $56$, and $61$. This conjecture concerns the detection of elements in the cokernel of the stable $\mathrm{J}$-homomorphism and would determine precisely the dimensions in which very exotic spheres occur. The low-dimensional computations of Isaksen, Wang, and Xu, together with work of Ravenel and recent results, verify it up to dimension $102$; the assertion remains open in general.
record.source_name: Prasit Bhattacharya, Irina Bobkova and J. D. Quigley, “New infinite families in the stable homotopy groups of spheres”, arXiv:2404.10062 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Uniform boundedness conjecture for fixers of finite primitive permutation groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite primitive permutation group on $\Omega$, with point stabiliser $H$, and define

$$
\rho_0(G):=\max\left\{\frac{|K|}{|H|\sqrt{|\Omega|}}:K\leqslant G\text{ is a fixer}\right\}.
$$

**Uniform boundedness conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $\rho_0(G)<c$ for all finite primitive permutation groups $G$.
This conjecture asserts that the largest fixer, normalized by the order of a point stabiliser and the square root of the permutation degree, is uniformly bounded across all finite primitive permutation groups. Its status is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Budaghyan–Carlet–Helleseth conjecture on the algebraic degree of APN functions
record.statement:
Let $F \colon \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be an almost perfect nonlinear (APN) function, meaning that for every $a,b \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $a \ne 0$, the equation $F(x+a)+F(x)=b$ has either zero or two solutions. The **algebraic degree** of $F$ is the maximum degree of a monomial appearing in its algebraic normal form.

**Budaghyan–Carlet–Helleseth conjecture.** No APN function $F \colon \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has algebraic degree $n$ for all $n \geq 3$.

APN functions are important in cryptography because they provide optimal resistance to differential attacks, and their graphs are Sidon sets. The conjecture is stated in the source as a completely open question.

record.title: Submaximal character degree ratio conjecture for symmetric groups
record.statement:
Let $b_1(n)$ be the largest irreducible character degree of the symmetric group $S_n$, and for each $m\geq 2$ let $b_m(n)$ be the $m$-th largest irreducible character degree of $S_n$. **Submaximal character degree ratio conjecture.** For any fixed integer $m\geq 2$,

$$
\frac{b_m(n)}{b_1(n)}\to 1\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

This conjecture asserts that symmetric groups have no single character degree that remains asymptotically separated from the other largest degrees; the paper presents experimental evidence for the analogous behavior of the second and third largest degrees, but does not provide a proof for arbitrary fixed $m$.

record.title: The recursive upper-bound conjecture for multidimensional egg-drop problems
record.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $N_1,N_2,\dots,N_d$ be the side lengths of a $d$-dimensional setting, and let $k$ be the number of eggs. Write $P_d(k)$ for the minimum number of drops required in the worst-case scenario under the strategy considered in the paper.

**Recursive upper-bound conjecture.** In a $d$-dimensional setting,

$$
P_d(k)\leq\left\lceil (k-d+1)\cdot(N_1+N_2+\dots+N_d)^{1/(k-d+1)}\right\rceil,
$$

for $k\geq d$.

The conjecture extrapolates the recursive upper bounds established in the one-, two-, and three-dimensional cases to arbitrary dimension. It concerns the performance of the same critical-point strategy in the worst case; the general $d$-dimensional claim is presented as suggested by the lower-dimensional pattern, with no resolution supplied here.
record.source_name: Xiangwen Cao, Zongyun Chen and Steven J. Miller, “Egg Drop Problems: They Are All They Are Cracked Up To Be!”, arXiv:2511.18330 (2025).

record.title: The sharp formula for non-trivially $t$-intersecting families
record.statement:
For integers $r\ge 3$ and $r-2\ge t\ge 1$, let $\iota_0(t,n;r)$ denote the maximum size of a $t$-intersecting family in an $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph with all parts of size $n$ and with total intersection of size less than $t$. **The sharp-formula conjecture.** If $n\ge 2$, then

$$
\iota_0(t,n;r)=\max\\{n^{r-t}-(n-1)^{r-t}+t(n-1),(t+2)n^{r-t-1}-(t+1)n^{r-t-2}\\}.
$$

For sufficiently large $n$, the paper proves this formula and identifies a phase transition at $t=\frac{r}{2}-1$; the conjecture asserts that the same extremal formula holds for every $n\ge 2$.

record.title: The optimality conjecture for induced odd cycles in planar graphs
record.statement: Let $k\geq 3$, and let $h_k(n)$ denote the number of induced copies of $C_{2k+1}$ obtained by evenly blowing up $k$ pairwise non-adjacent vertices in a $C_{2k+1}$ on $n$ vertices. For a planar graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\mathscr{H}(G,C_{2k+1})$ be the number of induced copies of $C_{2k+1}$ in $G$. **Optimality conjecture for induced odd cycles.** The maximum of $\mathscr{H}(G,C_{2k+1})$ over all planar graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices is $h_k(n)$. This construction gives the best currently known lower bound for the inducibility of odd cycles in planar graphs; its optimality remains open for all $k\geq 3$.

record.title: Wang's D-coloring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge4$.

**Wang's conjecture.** The D-coloring number of $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_D(G)\le
\begin{cases}
9, & \Delta=4,\\
10, & \Delta=5,\\
2\Delta-1, & \Delta\ge6.
\end{cases}
$$

The bound is motivated by planar book constructions and by known upper bounds for the related B-coloring problem; the conjecture remains open only for $6\le\Delta\le32$.

record.title: Rousseeuw and Hubert's conjecture on maximum regression depth
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in $d$-dimensional space. The **regression depth** of a hyperplane is the minimum number of points intersected by the hyperplane as it undergoes a continuous motion from its initial position to vertical. **Rousseeuw and Hubert's conjecture.** For every $d$-dimensional set of $n$ points, there exists a hyperplane having regression depth

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{d+1}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture asks for the higher-dimensional analogue of the optimal planar bound, and is motivated by the relation between regression depth and center-point phenomena. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: The half-turn symmetric alternating-sign-matrix enumeration conjecture for the D_r qKZ ground state
record.statement:
At the Razumov–Stroganov point $q=e^{2i\pi/3}$, take the homogeneous limit $w_i=1$ for all $i$ in the level-one $D_r$ $q$KZ solution, viewed as the Perron–Frobenius eigenvector $\Psi$ of the transfer-matrix Hamiltonian $H_D$. Normalize $\Psi$ so that its smallest entry is $\Psi_{\pi_0}=1$. **Half-turn symmetric alternating-sign-matrix conjecture.** The sum of the entries is the number of half-turn symmetric alternating sign matrices of size $r$:

$$
\sum_\pi\Psi_\pi=A_{HT}(r).
$$

This conjecture connects the homogeneous ground-state vector of the $D_r$ model with half-turn symmetric alternating sign matrices. The source presents the equality as a finding at the Razumov–Stroganov point and provides no proof or resolution.

record.title: Bernhard–Jablan conjecture on the unlinking number
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a link. Its **unlinking number** $u(L)$ is the minimum number of crossing changes needed to transform $L$ into an unlink, and $u_{BJ}(L)$ denotes its Bernhard–Jablan unlinking number. **Bernhard–Jablan conjecture.** For every link $L$ we have

$$
u(L)=u_{BJ}(L).
$$

The conjecture asserts equality between the classical unlinking number and the Bernhard–Jablan unlinking number; the supplied source does not establish whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Tight paths versus cliques
record.statement:
Improve the bounds. Is it $o(t^2)$? Perhaps the lower bound is the truth.

\emph{Related results:}

(Phelps--R\"odl) $r_3(P_2, K_t) = \Theta(t^2/\log t)$. This is the
same as giving the minimum independence number of a linear triple system on $n$ points.

(Mubayi--Cooper) $r_3(P_s,K_t) = \Theta(t^2)$ for fixed $s \geq 4$

Here is the construction giving the lower bound for $r_3(P_s,K_4)$ for
$s \geq 4$. Consider the 3-uniform $t^2$-vertex hypergraph with the vertex
set being points of a $t \times t$ grid, i.e., $V = [t] \times [t]$, and

$$
\{(x_1,y_2),(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_1)\} \quad \text{for all } 1 \le x_1 < x_2 \le t
\text{ and } 1 \le y_1 < y_2 \le t.

This hypergraph has independence number $2t -1$ and is $P_4$-free.

record.title: Second Eigenvalue Multiplicity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree bounded by $\Delta$. For the following choices of Hermitian matrix $M_G$ associated with $G$, what is the maximum multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue of $M_G$?
For the following choices of Hermitian matrix $M_G$ associated with $G$, what is the maximum multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue of $M_G$?
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item The adjacency matrix: in this case a sublinear upper bound was proved by, with an improvement in the case of regular graphs provided by and also for the normalized adjacency matrix of general bounded degree graphs. Constructions of graphs establishing lower bounds were given by.
 \item The Laplacian matrix.

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.35
record.statement: Determine the upper and lower estimates for the growth of entire and meromorphic solutions of algebraic ordinary differential equations (AODE). (This is a classical problem.) For AODEs of first order, it is known that the meromorphic solutions $f$ must have finite order (see Gol'dberg ) and that $(\log r)^2=O(T(r,f))$ (see Eremenko , ). (The latter two references contain a general account of first order AODEs, including modern proofs of some classical results.) The order of entire solutions of first order AODEs is an integral multiple of $\frac{1}{2}$ (see Malmquist ). For AODEs of second order, it is known that the order of entire solutions is positive, see Zimogljad . There is no upper estimate valid for all entire or meromorphic solutions of AODEs of order grreater than one, but there is an old conjecture that $\log |f(z)|\leq exp_n(|z|)$ for entire solutions $f$ of an AODE of order $n$. (A. Eremenko)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.31
record.statement: Erd\"os and Newman conjectured that if $$ f(z)=\sum^n_{k=0}a_kz^k,\hspace{1cm} |a_k|=1, \hspace{1cm}0\leq k\leq n, $$ then there is an absolute constant $c$ such that $$ \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)|>(1+c)n^{1/2}. $$ The weaker form of our conjecture stated that ([source label: D2]) holds if we assume \linebreak \mbox{$a_k=\pm1$} (Problem 4.13). A stronger form would be that ([source label: D2]) holds even if \mbox{$f(z)=\sum^n_{k=1}a_{n_k}z^{n_k}$}, $n_k$ natural numbers, $|a_{n_k}|=1$. However, ([source label: D2]) was disproved by Kahane (no citation). In fact, he showed that, given that $\varepsilon>0$, there are polynomials of the form ([source label: D1]) for which $$ \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)|<n^{1/2}+O(n^{(3/10)+\varepsilon})\hspace{1cm}\text{ as }n\to\infty. $$ Show that $n^{(3/10)+\varepsilon}$ cannot be replaced by $n^\varepsilon$ in ([source label: D3]). Is there any $n$-th degree polynomial of the form ([source label: D1]) for which $$ \min_{|z|=1}|f(z)|>(1-\varepsilon)n^{1/2} $$ for every positive $\varepsilon$ if $n>n_0(\varepsilon)$? Perhaps there is an $n$-th degree polynomial of the form ([source label: D1]), for which, for all $z$, $|z|=1$, $$ (1-\varepsilon)n^{1/2}<|f(z)|<(1+\varepsilon)n^{1/2}. $$ In fact, ([source label: D5]) could possibly hold with $n^{1/2}+O(1)$ on the left and right. It would be worthwhile to determine if ([source label: D2]) holds for $a_k=\pm1$ and for $a_{n_k}=\pm1$. (P. Erd\"os and D. Newman)

record.statement:
(The corona conjecture) Let $D$ be an arbitrary domain in the plane that supports non-constant bounded analytic functions. Suppose that $f_1(z),\ldots, f_n(z)$ are bounded and analytic in $D$ and satisfy \[\sum^n_{
u=1}|f_
u(z)|\geq\delta>0\] in $D$. Can one find bounded analytic functions $g_
u(z)$ in $D$ such that \[\sum^n_{
u=1}f_
u(z)g_
u(z)\equiv1\] in $D$? When $D$ is a disc, Carleson proved that the answer is `yes', and the result extends to finitely connected domains. record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.39
record.statement: Goluzin has shown that, if $g(z)\prec f(z)$ in $\mathbb{D}$, then \[M_2(r,g')\leq M_2(r,f'),\hspace{1cm}0\leq r\leq\frac{1}{2}.\] Here, for $p > 0$, \[M_p(r,h)=\Big(\frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{2\pi}_0|h(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta\Big)^{1/p}.\] The result is not necessarily true if $r > \frac{1}{2}$, as $f(z) = z, g(z) = z^2$ shows, though it follows from a theorem of Littlewood that, for all $p$, \[M_p(r,g)\leq M_p(r,f),\hspace{1cm} 0 < r < 1.\] Find the largest number $r_p, 0 < r_p < 1$, independent of $f$ and $g$ so that \[M_p(r,g')\leq M_p(r,f'),\hspace{1cm} 0<r<r_p,\] if $g\prec f$. Note: If $g(z) \prec f(z)$ in $\mathbb{D}$, then $g(z) = f(\phi(z))$ so that \[|g'(z)|\leq |f'(\phi(z))|,\hspace{1cm}|z|\leq\sqrt{2}-1,\] (see Carath\'eodory ). Thus if $h(z) = f'(\phi(z))$ then $h\prec f'$ so that, by Littlewood's theorem, $M_p(r,g') \leq M_p(r,h) \leq M_p(r,f')$ for $p > 0, r \leq\sqrt{2}-1$. This improves what one gets if one applied ([source label: C5.2]) to the $p$-th means since $\sqrt{2}-1>3-\sqrt{8}$; but it may not be best possible. (P. L. Duren)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.36
record.statement: This problem is equivalent to Problem 7.9 due to Gehring and Reich about best bounds for area distribution under quasiconformal mapping. Let $E$ denote a measurable subset of the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$, $m$ denote $2$-dimensional measure, and define \[f_E(z)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\int\int_E\frac{dm(w)}{(w-z)^2},\hspace{1cm}z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus E.\] Thus, $f_E$ is the $2$-dimensional Hilbert transform of the characteristic function of $E$. It follows from the Calder\'on-Zygmund theory of singular integrals that there are constants $a$ and $b$ such that \[\int\int_{\mathbb{D}\setminus E}|f_E|\,dm\leq am(E)\log\frac{\pi}{m(E)}+bm(E)\] for every $E$. The problem is to find the smallest possible $a$ (for which there exists some $b$ such that the inequality holds for every $E\subset\mathbb{D}$). Consideration of $E=\{z:|z|<\delta\}$ for small $\delta$ shows that $a=1$ would be best possible, and this is conjectured by Gehring and Reich. An analogous sharp inequality for sets $E\subset[-1,1]$ and $1$-dimensional Hilbert transforms \[f_E(x)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\int_E\frac{dt}{x-t}\] is known, and can be proved either by a subordination argument or by use of a theorem of Stein and Weiss. (A. Baernstein)

record.title: Virtual-knot problem 33 — Find a way to effectively compute the Kauffman–Radford–Hennings (KRH) invariants for three-manifolds via right integr…
record.statement:
Find a way to effectively compute the Kauffman–Radford–Hennings
(KRH) invariants for three-manifolds via right
integrals on finite dimensional Hopf algebras . Find a way
to categorify the Kauffman–Radford–Hennings invariants for all
finite dimensional quasitriangular Hopf algebras. The KRH invariants
are actually invariants of rotational virtual links that are also,
after normalization, invariant under the moves of the Kirby
calculus. In this way, they give invariants of three manifolds and
virtual three manifolds. The formulation of the KRH invariants in
terms of integrals for finite dimensional Hopf algebras is very
elegant, but computation is very difficult. Thus these invariants
form a challenge for both virtual and classical knot theory. It is
worth pointing out again, that the proper domain for all
quantum link invariants is rotational virtual knot theory. Thus,
this problem about the KRH invariants is a test case for the
structure of quantum link invariants as a whole.

record.title: Virtual-knot problem 53 — Is there any algorithm for recognition whether two graph-links are equivalent or not?
record.statement:
Is there any algorithm for recognition whether two graph-links are
equivalent or not? Our conjecture is “no”. The idea behind that is
that graph-links are complicated enough, and possibly, they contain
sufficiently many degrees of freedom to include something like
Turing machines. All mathematics is roughly split into the
recognizable one (low-dimensional topology, hyperbolic groups,
decidability) and the non-recognizable one (topology of dimension
$4$ and higher, arbitrary finitely presentable groups, Turing
machines etc). The usual argument for undecidability for finitely
presented group allows one to construct some universal (semi)groups
which includes the apparatus of the Turing machines. We think that
graph-links are enough complicated to include similar things: they
contain arbitrary graphs, and Reidemeister moves, in principle,
could play the role of “rules for formal languages” or “group
relations”. It seems unlikely that Reidemeister moves collapse
graph-links to anything simple enough because of the parity
considerations: there are “irreducibly odd” graph-links which are
stable in the sense that every equivalent graph contains the initial
graph as a subgraph.

record.title: Problem 5.25 — (Presentation for level L structures).
record.statement: (Presentation for level L structures). Give an explicit finite presentation for Modg[L]. Once one has such a presentation, it seems likely that it would fit well into the framework of Pitsch’s proof [ Pi] that rank( H2(Modg,1, Z))≤ 1 for g≥ 4. Note that Pitsch’s proof was extended to punctured and bordered case by Korkmaz-Stipsicsz; see [ Ko]. What Pitsch does is to begin with an explicit, finite presentation of Mod g,1, and then to apply Hopf’s formula for groups Γ presented as the quotient of a free group F by the normal closure R of the relators: H2(Γ, Z) = R∩ [F,F ] [F,R ] (17) In other words, elements of H2(Γ, Z) come precisely from commutators which are relators, except for the trivial ones. Amazingly, one needs only write the form of an arbitrary element of the numerator in (17), and a few tricks reduces the computation of (an upper bound for) space of solutions to computing the rank of an integer matrix. In our case this approach seems feasible, especially with computer computation, at least for small L. Of course one hopes to find a general pattern.

record.statement: Find explicit way of calculating d1(ϕ) for any given element ϕ ∈ Kg. In particular, determine whether the Magnus representation Ig,1→GL(2g; Z[H]) of the Torelli group detectsd1 or not. Suzuki [ 103] proved that the Magnus representation of the Torelli group mentioned above is not faithful so that it may happen that the intersection of the kernel of the Magnus representation withKg is not contained in the kernel of d1. We may also ask whether the representation of the hyperelliptic mapping class group given by Jones [ 45], restricted to the intersection of this group withKg, detects d1 or not (cf. Kasahara [ 46] for a related work for the case g = 2). There are also various interesting works related to the class d1 such as Endo [ 14] and Morifuji [ 71] treating the hyperelliptic mapping class group, Kitano [ 54] as well as Hain and Reed [ 33]. Recently Biss and Farb [ 5] proved that the group Kg is not finitely generated for all g≥ 3 (K2 is known to be an infinitely generated free group by Mess [ 69]). However it is still not yet known whether the abelianization H1(Kg) is finitely generated or not (cf. Problem 2.2 of [ 80]). Finally we would like to mention that Kawazumi [ 50] is developing a theory of harmonic Mag- nus expansions which gives in particular a system of diﬀerential forms representing the Mumford- Morita-Miller classes on the universal family of curves over the moduli space Mg.
